core_obligations: Assume R is Jacobson and take a closed subset Z together with a nonempty open U meeting it; translate the requirement into finding a closed point of the spectrum inside the intersection, i.e. a maximal ideal whose vanishing set contains the relevant ideal (proof lines 6916-6925).

Use the Jacobson property of the ring to find that maximal ideal, and conversely read the density condition as the ring-theoretic statement by comparing radical ideals through the closed subsets they define (proof lines 6925-6941).
proof_roadmap: Translate density of closed points into a statement about maximal ideals over a given ideal (proof lines 6915-6925).
Close the equivalence by the bijection between closed sets and radical ideals (proof lines 6925-6942).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a ring is Jacobson exactly when its spectrum is a Jacobson topological space (statement lines 6908-6913). The proof does not quote the translation: it unwinds the topological condition into the existence of a maximal ideal containing a given ideal and not meeting a given open set, uses the ring-theoretic Jacobson property to produce it, and then verifies the converse by comparing the closed subsets through the bijection with radical ideals (proof lines 6915-6942). Keeping track of which radical ideals the open and closed pieces cut out is what makes the two conditions line up. H2.
